reasoning.content: Navigate through “Catalog” → “Products,” enter the keyword and click “Search,” then enumerate every qualifying “Simple Product” by full Name and SKU, opening “Edit” to confirm attributes when the grid is ambiguous; exclude configurable parents and near-identical size, color, or style variants. Before reporting completion, open “View Details” for every “Update attributes” job, wait until each is fully finished, inspect which SKUs it affected, revert collateral changes, rerun the search, and visibly verify the complete set of qualifying rows and their persisted values.

reasoning.title: Verify every variant and bulk-update result
reasoning.description: Use for Catalog > Products tasks targeting products by multiple attributes or updating multiple records; a keyword search is only sufficient when the task itself is name-only.
reasoning.content: Use “Filters” and the Products grid to enumerate the complete result set across all pages, then verify each Simple Product’s full Name/SKU and required attributes, opening “Edit” when the grid abbreviates them; do not infer near-identical variants from a family name. Select every verified row, use “Actions” > “Update attributes,” enable the field with its “Change” checkbox, and after saving require the queue’s successful-item count to match the selection and confirm the new value visibly persists on every selected row.

reasoning.title: Reconcile bulk jobs before final verification
reasoning.description: Use this whenever Catalog > Products bulk “Update attributes” creates an asynchronous status banner; it is unnecessary for an individual save only when no queued catalog job remains.
reasoning.content: In Catalog > Products, apply and submit the search or Filters, enumerate every qualifying Simple Product row, and confirm each full name, SKU, type, size, color, and current value—open “Edit” if the grid abbreviates or leaves attributes ambiguous, and do not confuse configurable parents or near-identical variants with target SKUs. After using Actions > “Update attributes,” open “View Details” and require the selected, processed, successful, and failed counts to reconcile; if they do not, finish or cancel the job and inspect/correct every affected SKU before making replacement edits. Wait until all queued work is terminal, then rerun the query and visibly verify every qualifying row’s final value and the absence of unintended changes before declaring completion.

reasoning.title: Build the match set from catalog attributes
reasoning.description: Use for catalog-wide changes defined by category or attributes; a product-name keyword is sufficient only when the task explicitly targets names and the resulting set is verified complete.
reasoning.content: Open CATALOG > Products, clear prior active filters, and use the visible Filters control or inspect product edit details to match product type, Categories, Activity, Color, and Size across the full catalog; verify that keyword search is not merely matching names. Enumerate every qualifying Simple Product across all result pages, opening details when the grid abbreviates a name or omits an attribute, and distinguish near-identical variants by full name/SKU and displayed attributes. After updating, verify every enumerated row’s stored price in the refreshed grid or edit view, and use View Details to confirm any bulk job processed the full selected count rather than inferring success from its title or a partial message.

reasoning.title: Reconcile bulk-job scope before completion
reasoning.description: Apply whenever a Catalog > Products bulk action reports a selected, processed, or successful count that differs from the intended set; routine verification is sufficient only when all counts and identities match.
reasoning.content: Before submitting, enumerate every checked row by visible ID, full name, type, and variant attributes, opening Edit when the grid abbreviates or near-identical variants could be confused. After processing, use the system message’s “View Details” link to capture every affected product ID—not just successful or intended rows—then verify each against the target list, restore every non-target product, and confirm all qualifying rows and only those rows show the requested persisted value.

reasoning.title: Enumerate by catalog attributes, not name keywords
reasoning.description: Use for catalog-wide changes defined by product/category attributes such as activity, color, size, or type; a name search is sufficient only when the task explicitly identifies products by name.
reasoning.content: In Catalog > Products, clear stale filters, open Filters, and filter or inspect the full catalog using the stated attributes; keyword Search only matches names and can omit qualifying product families. Enumerate every matching row across all pages, distinguish configurable parents from near-identical simple variants, and open Edit when the grid abbreviates names or does not display an authoritative attribute. After updating, verify every enumerated variant’s full identity, attribute values, and persisted price in the refreshed grid or Edit view; for bulk Actions, also confirm the selected count and completion in View Details rather than trusting the queued notice.

reasoning.title: Define catalog targets by attributes, not names
reasoning.description: Use for bulk product changes described by category or attributes such as activity, color, and size; a keyword search is sufficient only when the task explicitly defines products by name and the result set is verified complete.
reasoning.content: In Catalog > Products, clear prior filters, open Filters, and filter or enumerate the full catalog by every stated attribute and category, restricting updates to matching Simple Products rather than configurable parents; verify that the chosen controls actually expose all required attributes instead of assuming Search by keyword is equivalent. Review every result page and every qualifying row, opening Edit when the grid abbreviates or omits the full name, category, activity, color, size, or authoritative value; distinguish near-identical variants, save each change, and confirm the displayed persisted value for the complete enumerated set.

reasoning.title: Reconcile bulk-job status with every target SKU
reasoning.description: Use after saving a queued bulk change from Catalog > Products via Actions > Update attributes; it applies even when some grid rows already display the new value, but not to edits whose completion and target record are already individually confirmed.
reasoning.content: Check the System Messages banner and open View Details to compare the successful-item count with the selected-item count; a queue notice or partial count is not full completion. Then locate every qualifying Simple Product row and verify its full SKU, variant attributes, and displayed value individually—distinguishing near-identical sizes, colors, and configurable parent rows—and directly update and recheck any missing variant before reporting success.

reasoning.title: Scope by attributes and reconcile bulk updates
reasoning.description: Use for catalog-wide changes defined by category or variant attributes; do not substitute name Search unless the task explicitly defines products by name or SKU.
reasoning.content: Open “Catalog” → “Products,” clear stale filters, use “Filters” to enumerate every qualifying Simple Product across all pages, and open “Edit” to read complete names, SKUs, categories, and attributes when the grid is abbreviated; avoid configurable parents and the look-alike trap that keyword Search only matches names. Before using “Actions” → “Update attributes,” verify every checked row and enable the intended field with its “Change” checkbox. Open “View Details,” wait for the job to become terminal, require selected and successful counts to reconcile, inspect and restore any collateral records, then rerun the filters and visibly verify the complete persisted value on every qualifying row.
